name: Thymic Neuroendocrine Carcinoma

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of neuroendocrine carcinoma in thymic tissue
Positive staining for neuroendocrine markers such as chromogranin A, synaptophysin, and CD56
Radiologic evidence of anterior mediastinal mass consistent with thymic origin
Exclusion of metastatic neuroendocrine carcinoma from other primary sites

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with positive neuroendocrine markers and exclusion of metastatic disease
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including pathology, radiology, and clinical correlation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Anterior mediastinal mass detected on imaging
pathognomonic.notes: Often identified incidentally or due to mass effect
searchTerms: mass in front of chest detected by scan

pathognomonic.symptomName: Paraneoplastic Cushing syndrome due to ectopic ACTH secretion
pathognomonic.notes: Occurs in a subset of functional tumors
searchTerms: excess cortisol due to tumor hormone

common.symptomName: Chest pain localized to anterior mediastinum
common.notes: Due to tumor invasion or compression
searchTerms: chest pain in front of chest
unintentional weight loss and poor appetite

occasional.notes: Due to vascular compression by tumor

occasional.symptomName: Hoarseness from recurrent laryngeal nerve involvement
searchTerms: voice changes due to recurrent laryngeal nerve

occasional.notes: Seen in functional tumors secreting serotonin or other peptides

rare.notes: Autoimmune neuromuscular disorder associated with neuroendocrine tumors
searchTerms: autoimmune muscle weakness related to cancer

rare.symptomName: Hypoglycemia due to insulin-like peptide secretion
searchTerms: low blood sugar from insulin-like hormone
blood sugar drops caused by insulin-like peptide

rare.notes: Due to tumor invasion or inflammation

laboratory: Elevated serum ACTH in functional tumors
Increased chromogranin A and neuron-specific enolase levels
Possible electrolyte abnormalities related to paraneoplastic syndromes
imaging: CT or MRI showing anterior mediastinal mass with possible invasion
PET scan demonstrating metabolic activity consistent with malignancy
genetic: Possible MEN1 gene mutations in familial cases
No specific recurrent genetic alterations established
other: Histopathology showing neuroendocrine morphology with mitotic activity
Immunohistochemical positivity for synaptophysin, chromogranin, CD56

distinguishingFeatures: Clinical and imaging evidence of other primary sites

redFlags: Signs of superior vena cava syndrome
Paraneoplastic endocrine syndromes such as Cushing syndrome
references: Travis WD et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Lung, Pleura, Thymus and Heart. IARC; 2021.
Filosso PL et al. Thymic neuroendocrine tumors: clinical features and treatment outcomes. Ann Thorac Surg. 2015.
